content.title: Volcano Ice Intervention | Helicopter Scale, Active Drop and Eruption Response
content.summary: An adult volcanologist drops one mineral block and observes a vent reaction return to the aircraft. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.

quick_start.input_format: Exactly three clearly adult miniature workers retain identity and scale. + Each task step uses visible tools and contact. + The giant table geography remains continuous. + A full-size hand enters only once at the terminal interruption. + The slack rope proves the direct consequence of the removed object.
quick_start.recommended_input: An adult volcanologist holds one large blue mineral block at an open survey aircraft door above a copper geothermal vent. On contact, create one blue cooling disk at the center while a copper liquid ring begins rotating around it. Return to the same aircraft doorway as the white plume reaches it; the volcanologist crouches once behind the door frame.
required_anchors: One clearly adult operator, one aircraft and one inert block persist.
The block is released exactly once and remains traceable to impact.
The crater or vent geography never resets during escalation.
The terminal cabin response is caused by the same plume.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: An adult volcanologist drops one mineral block and observes a vent reaction return to the aircraft. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
